predecessors.name: Sultanate of Rum
predecessors.text: the Taurus castles of Ermenek, Mut, Ereğli, Gülnar and Silifke, and Larende, held from the Seljuks of Rum (infobox 'Preceded by: Sultanate of Rum')

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Karaman Eyalet, 'founded from former territories of Karamanids': the plateau (Konya, Larende) annexed 1468, the Taurus rump at Silifke in 1487

ledger.x: c. 1255: Karaman Bey founds the Karamanid principality in the Taurus. Infobox 'Established: c. 1255'; 'Karaman Bey expanded his territories by capturing castles in Ermenek, Mut, Ereğli, Gülnar, and Silifke' (the page's 1225 for these conquests 'seems excessively early'). The Anatolian beyliks table has the rule from…
c. 1260: Kilij Arslan IV gives the Karamanids Larende and Ermenek. 'he gave the town of Larende (now Karaman, in honour of the dynasty) and Ermenek (c. 1260)'.
1260: Mut passes to the Karamanids.
12 May 1277: Mehmed Bey takes Konya from the Seljuks of Rum.
1278: the Karamanid hold on Konya ends.
1305 (a reading): the Karamanids are drawn as an Ilkhanid dependency, mirroring the ilkhanate dossier's vassal_start of 1305 (confidence 1, Cliopatria's year).
1307: the Karamanid seat moves to Konya (infobox 'Konya (1307–1468)'); the conquest of Konya is dated 1308 on the same infobox.
1308: the Karamanids conquer Konya and the Seljuk plateau.
1326 (page silent): Cliopatria adds a strip west of the core (Lake Beyşehir and the country west of it) in the year its Eshrefids row ends.
1330s: the Karamanids expand as the Ilkhanids fall.
30 November 1335: Abu Said dies and the Ilkhanid governorship of Anatolia ends with him.
1352 (page silent): the north-western strip drops out of Cliopatria's shape for ten years, to no other Cliopatria state.
1363 (page silent): the strip north-west of Konya returns to Cliopatria's shape under Alaattin Ali (table 1361-1398); no page opened names the land or the neighbour (confidence 1).
1390 (summer and fall): Bayezid I takes Akşehir, Niğde and the capital Konya from the Karamanids.
1390 (a reading): with Konya lost the Karamanid seat falls back on Larende (Karaman), the infobox's first-listed capital; the Bayezid I page names no new seat.
1391 (a bridge over a silence): peace with Bayezid I.
1391 (a reading, with the gain above): the seat returns to Konya (infobox 'Konya (1307–1468)').
1397: Bayezid I defeats the Karamanids at Akçay and annexes their territory.
1402: Timur restores the Karamanid lands after Ankara.
September 1410: war between Karaman and Germiyan.
1411: Kütahya falls to Mehmed II of Karaman and the fighting ends in a Karamanid hold; no treaty is on the page.
1411: Mehmed II of Karaman takes Kütahya.
1414: Kütahya returns to Germiyan.
1466: Mehmed II takes Larende and Konya.
1468: the Ottomans annex Konya and the plateau.
1468: Konya and the plateau pass to the Ottomans; the Karamanids keep the Taurus coast.
1474: the rump state's seat is Silifke (infobox 'Silifke (1474–1487)'; 'Rump state (1474-1487)').
1487: the Ottomans take the last Karamanid land.
1487: the Karamanid state ends.

wars.name: Karamanid capture of Konya (1277)
wars.outcome: The Karamanids take Konya on 12 May 1277 and install a pretender; Mehmed Bey is 'defeated by Seljuq and Mongol forces and executed with some of his brothers in 1278'.

wars.name: Bayezid I's campaigns against the Karamanids
wars.outcome: In the summer and fall of 1390 Bayezid took Akşehir, Niğde and 'their capital Konya from the Karaman'; he 'accepted peace proposals from Karaman (1391)' (no terms on the page) before turning on Kastamonu; in 1397 he defeated and killed the emir at Akçay and…

wars.name: Battle of Ankara and the Timurid restoration of Karaman
wars.outcome: Bayezid I's army is defeated on 20 July 1402 (Bayezid I page: 'In 1400, Timur succeeded in rousing the local Turkic beyliks'); Timur gives the Karamanid lands to Mehmed Bey.

wars.name: Murad II's campaigns against the Karamanids
wars.outcome: 'The Karamanids were defeated in 1428' and the infobox lists 'Campaign in Karamanids (1444)'; the page names no land that changed hands.

wars.name: Mehmed II's conquest of Karaman
wars.outcome: Mehmed II captures Karaman (Larende) and Konya in 1466 (Mehmed II page); the Karamanids infobox dates the annexation of Konya to 1468, a rump state at Silifke 1474-1487, and the end of the state to the Ottomans in 1487.

wars.name: Karaman, Germiyan and the Ottomans over Kütahya (1410-1415)
wars.outcome: War between Karaman and Germiyan from September 1410; Kütahya falls to Mehmed II of Karaman in 1411 and Mehmed Çelebi reinstates Yakub in Germiyan in 1414 (Germiyanids page); the Karamanids infobox gives an 'Ottoman-Karamanid War' of 1413-1415.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or a survey for the Karamanids; the Taurus, plateau and western frontiers are approximate throughout.
